title: Optimal \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) distortion of edit distance
formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(n\to \infty , D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)=\inf \{D\ge 1: \exists m\ge 1, f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to \mathbb{R} ^{m}, a>0, \forall x,y, a\cdot ED(x,y)\le \Vert f(x)- f(y)\Vert _{1}\le D a\cdot ED(x,y)\}\), for integers \(n\ge 2\).
definitions: ED is Levenshtein distance with unit-cost insertion, deletion and substitution; intermediate strings may have other lengths. The \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) norm is the sum of absolute coordinate values. The dimension m is any finite positive integer and the map has arbitrary real coordinates. Neither dimension nor construction/evaluation time is bounded. The scale a and map may depend on n. The infimum is over all such embeddings and common scales, with the inequalities holding simultaneously for every pair. Every finite metric admits a finite-distortion embedding, so \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\) is finite. The target concerns metric existence, not running time of string comparison.

context_blocks.text: The quantitative target is the growth of the best distortion. The previous question asked only whether that growth can be bounded by a fixed power of log n.

An embedding compares a difficult sequence metric with the additive geometry of \(\ell\)\(_{1}\). Polylogarithmic distortion would sharply improve the known structural representation of edit distance.

The Ostrovsky–Rabani construction gives subpolynomial distortion that is larger than polylogarithmic. The existence target is distinct from fast approximation algorithms: a nonconstructive embedding need not be efficiently evaluable. The convention includes substitutions explicitly.

why: Resolve a central metric-embedding barrier for sequence comparison.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function \(h(n)\) and absolute constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \(c h(n)\le D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\le C h(n)\) for all \(n\ge 2\), and prove the matching embedding and obstruction bounds in Lean. The bounds must concern unrestricted finite-dimensional \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) embeddings in the stated edit convention. Establishing only a polylogarithmic upper bound need not determine the requested asymptotic order.

sentences: Edit distance counts unit-cost insertions, deletions and substitutions between binary strings.
An \(\ell\)\(_{1}\) embedding represents those distances by sums of coordinate differences, up to a common multiplicative distortion.
The target is the smallest distortion as a function of string length, within constant factors.
Embedding dimension and construction time are unrestricted.
The earlier polylogarithmic-distortion question selects one possible growth regime of this extremal function.
